job.title: Learning Enhancement Assistant
job.description:
About Us:
Nestled within the picturesque landscapes of the Mornington Peninsula, Toorak Colleges’ reputation in innovation and limitless possibilities is what sees it continue to be a choice destination for educators.  With a legacy spanning 150 years, we remain committed to igniting curiosity and empowering students to thrive in the modern world.  With beautiful grounds and a connected community, Toorak College provides an ideal environment for both students, educators and operational staff to work together to bring about the change we wish to see in the world tomorrow.

At Toorak College, our Learning Enhancement team works collaboratively with teachers, students and families to support individual learning needs and ensure every student has the opportunity to engage positively and achieve their potential.

Role and Responsibilities:
As a Learning Enhancement Assistant, you will work collaboratively with classroom teachers and the Learning Enhancement team to support students within the Senior School. The role will focus on providing individual and small-group support, assisting students to engage with classroom learning and working towards the goals outlined in their individual learning plans. 

Key responsibilities include:
  • Supporting classroom teachers with the implementation of learning programs and classroom activities.
  • Working with individual students and small groups to support engagement, participation and learning outcomes.
  • Supporting students to work towards the goals outline in their individual learning plans.
  • Assisting students with additional learning needs to access and participate in classroom learning.
  • Observing and documenting student progress and development as directed by the classroom teacher.
  • Supporting the use of technology to enhance student learning and engagement.
  • Providing student supervision and pastoral support as required.
  • Assisting with classroom administration and other learning-related activities.
  • Developing  positive and supportive relationships with students.
  • Working collaboratively with classroom teachers, Year Level Learning teams and the Learning Enhancement team.
  • Maintaining professional and confidential communication with students, staff and families.
This is a permanent part-time position (FTE 0.6) commencing at the start of the 2027 School Year. Experience supporting students with additional learning needs, diverse learning profiles or individual learning plans will be highly regarded.

About You:
You are passionate about supporting young people and enjoy helping students develop confidence, independence and positive approaches to learning. You are patient, approachable and able to build strong and respectful relationships with students while working collaboratively with teachers and the Learning Enhancement team.

You will ideally have:
  • An understanding of the diverse learning needs of students and a willingness to adapt support accordingly.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to connect positively with students.
  • The ability to work collaboratively with classroom teachers and the Learning Enhancement team.
  • A calm, patient and flexible approach to supporting student learning.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to follow direction while also demonstrating initiative. 
  • Confidence using technology to support student learning.
  • A commitment to maintaining student confidentiality and professional boundaries.
Relevant qualifications or experience in education, learning support, teacher assistance, youth work or a related field will be advantageous. Candidates with a genuine passion for supporting young people and relevant experience are encouraged to apply.

Why Choose Toorak College?
  • Beautiful Mornington Peninsula location - a walk from the beach.
  • Toorak College staff have access to our onsite Athletics and Gym facilities.
  • On-site cafe and regularly catered Morning Teas and Lunches for staff.
  • Toorak College prides itself on a supportive and collegial culture among staff and students.
  • Utilise cutting-edge facilities and resources.
  • Access to our outstanding Employee Assistance Program.
Application Process:
 If you’re ready to join our team, we want to hear from you! You can find out more about us at www.careers.toorakcollege.vic.edu.au 

Please submit a two (2) page resume, covering letter, including the name and contact details of two (2) confidential referees.  Your application should be addressed to Mrs Kristy Kendall, School Principal, Toorak College.

Please note: You MUST have full working rights in Australia and a current Working with Children Check (Employer) to apply for this position.

The closing date for applications is 9:00am 12th October 2026.
  
We would like to inform potential applicants that the role may close earlier if we receive a high volume of suitable candidates.  We encourage candidates to submit applications early, as interviews may commence prior to the closing date.  Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted at the time of shortlisting, all applications will be acknowledged at the conclusion of the process.

Toorak College is committed to a Child Safe school environment, and we have extensive recruitment and screening processes in place. All interested applicants are encouraged to read and familiarise themselves with Toorak Colleges' Child Safety and Wellbeing Policy located on the Toorak College website. Toorak College is a child safe organisation which welcomes all children, young people and their families. Toorak College is committed to the safety and wellbeing of all children, including those under the care and supervision of the School.

The School recognises the importance of, and its responsibility for, ensuring a safe and supportive environment which respects the rights of children and fosters their enrichment and wellbeing. Toorak College is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to establishing a welcoming and inclusive environment for all members of the School Community.

job.title: Performing Arts, Dance & Aerobics Coordinator
job.description:
About Us:
Nestled within the picturesque landscapes of the Mornington Peninsula, Toorak College empowers our students through academic and personal growth so they will thrive in their future. With a legacy spanning 150 years, we remain committed to igniting curiosity and empowering students to shine in the world beyond our gates. With state-of-the-art facilities and a close-knit community, Toorak College provides an ideal environment for both students and staff to thrive.

Our Performing Arts programs provide students with opportunities to develop confidence, creativity, collaboration and performance skills through a diverse range of co-curricular activities. From Dance and Drama through to Aerobics, Dancestar and our Toorak Academy of Performing Arts (TAPA), students are encouraged to explore their talents, challenge themselves and participate in a vibrant and supportive performance community.

Role and Responsibilities:
As the Performing Arts, Dance & Aerobics Coordinator at Toorak College, you will provide coordination and administrative support across the School’s Performing Arts and competitive performance programs, ensuring their smooth and effective operation. This role is part-time, fixed term for Term 1, 2027, providing long service leave cover. The role may be made larger by taking on coaching opportunities across the term.
  
Working collaboratively with staff, coaches, students and families, you will:
  • Coordinate TAPA, Aerobics and Dancestar programs across Prep–Year 12, including coach allocations, relief coverage, registrations, teams, schedules and competition preparation.
  • Coordinate the School’s Aerobics and Dancestar programs across Years 3 – 12, including coach allocations, relief coverage, student registrations, teams, schedules and competition preparation.
  • Provide ongoing support, guidance and coordination to the coaching team, promoting a consistent and effective approach across programs.
  • Lead the administrative and organisational requirements associated with the School Musical, working closely with the Director and Director of Music.
  • Coordinate key events including the Aerobics and Dancestar Display Night and Team Sunday rehearsal.
  • Manage registrations, team entries, music uploads and competition schedules through relevant external portals.
  • Maintain accurate student teams, attendance records, calendars, schedules and program information across Veracross and other relevant systems.
  • Oversee program budgets, resources, costumes, props, equipment and first-aid requirements.
  • Lead communication with students and families regarding TAPA, Aerobics, Dancestar and the School Musical.
  • Coordinate activity registrations, payments and selections in conjunction with the relevant co-curricular support teams.
  • Maintain effective communication and liaison with staff, students, families and external organisations to ensure programs and events are well organised and successfully delivered; and
  • Contribute to the promotion and profile of Dance, Drama and Performing Arts across the School.
About You:
You are an organised and proactive professional with a genuine passion for Performing Arts and experience coordinating programs, events or activities in a school or similar environment. You will be confident in managing multiple priorities, communicating with a diverse range of stakeholders and ensuring the administrative and operational requirements of programs are delivered efficiently. You will bring strong attention to detail, excellent organisational and communication skills, and the ability to work collaboratively with staff, coaches, students, families and external providers. You will be adaptable, solutions-focused and comfortable taking initiative in a busy and varied environment. Experience in Performing Arts, Dance, Aerobics, event management or co-curricular program coordination within an education environment will be highly regarded.

Qualifications and Requirements:
  • Relevant qualification in Performing Arts, Dance or a related discipline, with additional training in Arts, Event or Program Management desirable.
  • Experience coordinating Performing Arts, Dance, Aerobics, events or co-curricular programs, with relevant program or event management experience highly regarded.
  • Current Working with Children Check – Employer.
  • Strong organisational, administrative and project coordination skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with staff, students, families and external providers.
Why Choose Toorak College?
  • Beautiful Mornington Peninsula location – work within your community.
  • Toorak College staff have access to our onsite Athletics and Gym facilities.
  • On-site café and regular catered Morning Teas and Lunches for staff.
  • Toorak College prides itself on a supportive and collegial culture among staff and students.
  • Utilise cutting-edge facilities and resources.
  • Access to our outstanding Employee Assistance Program.
Application Process:
If you’re ready to join our team, we want to hear from you!  Please submit a 2-page resume, cover letter, and the name and the contact details of two (2) confidential referees.  Your application should be addressed to Mrs Kristy Kendall, School Principal, Toorak College.
  
You can find out more about us at www.careers.toorakcollege.vic.edu.au 
  
Please note: You MUST have full working rights in Australia and a current Working With Children Check - Employer to apply.

The closing date for applications is 9:00am 12th October 2026.
  
We would like to inform potential applicants that the role may close earlier if we receive a high volume of suitable candidates. We encourage candidates to submit applications early, as interviews may commence prior to the closing date. Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

job.title: Risk and Compliance Officer
job.description:
About Us:
Nestled within the picturesque landscapes of the Mornington Peninsula, Toorak Colleges’ reputation in innovation and limitless possibilities is what sees it continue to be a choice destination for educators.  With a legacy spanning 150 years, we remain committed to igniting curiosity and empowering students to thrive in the modern world.  With beautiful grounds and a connected community, Toorak College provides an ideal environment for both students, educators and operational staff to work together to bring about the change we wish to see in the world tomorrow.

Role and Responsibilities:
The Risk and Compliance Officer plays a key role in supporting the effective management of risk, compliance and governance practices across the School.  This position is responsible for coordinating and monitoring the School’s risk and compliance frameworks, ensuring policies, procedures, audits and legislative obligations are effectively maintained and, where required, implemented.  Working collaboratively with leaders and staff across the School, the Risk and Compliance Officer will build strong and trusted relationships internally and externally, including regulatory bodies and other relevant authorities, providing expert advice and guidance to promote a proactive culture of safety, accountability and continuous improvement.
   
This is an exciting opportunity for a people focussed and experienced compliance professional looking for a part-time position who can lead and influence others to strengthen risk and compliance practices across the School.  Working collaboratively and proactively across the School, the successful candidate will draw on their in-depth compliance knowledge and strong influencing skills to build consensus, achieve a united approach and foster a culture of shared responsibility.

Key Responsibilities Include:
  • Lead the Education Team in reviewing, evaluating and approving risk assessments for all domestic and international camps, excursions and school events, as well as be the main point of contact for external bodies and stakeholders around student and staff safety.
  • Support the Executive and Senior Leadership Teams with the continuing implementation and ongoing review of the School's risk management and compliance frameworks.
  • Develop, maintain and monitor compliance registers, reporting processes and documentation to ensure regulatory obligations are met.
  • Coordinate risk assessments, compliance reviews and internal audits, ensuring identified actions are appropriately recorded, monitored and implemented.
  • Monitor legislative, regulatory and sector requirements relevant to the School and provide timely advice and updates to key stakeholders.
  • Support the development, review and implementation of School policies, procedures and operational guidelines.
  • Prepare risk, compliance and governance reports as required.
  • Partner with the Senior Leadership Team and all staff across the School to embed a strong risk-aware culture and promote continuous improvement.
  • Support emergency management planning, business continuity processes and associated compliance requirements.
  • Assist with compliance obligations relating to child safety, workplace health and safety, privacy and other areas of regulatory responsibility.
  • Maintain accurate records and documentation to support transparency, accountability and effective governance.
About You:
The successful candidate will be an experienced Risk and Compliance professional who demonstrates:
  • Strong influencing and relationship building skills and a capacity to work with large teams across various sectors of the organisation.
  • A strong understanding of risk management principles, compliance frameworks and governance practices.
  • Experience developing, implementing and reviewing policies, procedures and compliance processes.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret information, identify risks and provide practical recommendations.
  • Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, meet deadlines and maintain a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Outstanding interpersonal communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to influence across all levels and build positive relationships across the School.
  • A proactive and solutions-focused approach, with the ability to work independently while contributing positively as part of the broader School community.
Qualifications and Requirements:
  • Degree qualified or relevant qualifications in risk management, compliance, governance, business, law or a related discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience in a risk, compliance, governance, assurance or quality role.
  • Experience within an Education, Not-For-Profit or similarly regulated environment will be highly regarded.
  • Knowledge and understanding of legislative and regulatory requirements relevant to schools.
  • Commitment to upholding child safety standards and contributing to a culture of wellbeing and inclusion.
  • Current Working with Children Check - Employer.
Why Choose Toorak College?
  • Beautiful Mornington Peninsula location - work within your community.
  • Toorak College staff have access to our onsite Athletics and Gym facilities.
  • Toorak College prides itself on a supportive and collegial culture among staff and students.
  • Access to our outstanding Employee Assistance Program.
You can find out more about us at www.careers.toorakcollege.vic.edu.au

Application Process:
Please submit a 2-page resume, cover letter, and the name and the contact details of two confidential referees.  Your application should be addressed to Mrs Kristy Kendall, School Principal, Toorak College.

Please note: You must have full working rights to work in Australia to apply for this position.

The closing date for applications is 9am 12th October 2026
